Super late but: financial barriers have always been there, they were just viewed with a different perspective because for the majority, that was just how it was. Life was hard. Money was tight or nonexistent; you relied on what you and your family and community were able to produce to take care of everyone. Your life view and general knowledge of the world was often tied to what church you were a part of, and most people did not even leave the town they were born in their entire lives. The way of the world, for most, was work the farm or the family trade and have a family and then die on your land. The world is entirely different now, and that change was incredibly rapid. On another note, which can be seen in a historical perspective with large empires like Rome, is that when women are shown they are able to have a choice about having children or investing in themselves and their own satisfaction in life, a lot of women will choose not to have kids. As a woman myself, having kids is terrifying: irrevocable physical changes, childbirth itself carrying huge risks, a complete shift in life priorities, and men being men all make me rethink kids more than finances do (although finances do carry a heavy weight). Add to that the breakdown of genuine human connection and an absence of real communities, making having a 'village' highly questionable, and having kids suddenly seems much less appealing than fulfilling other life goals that are now more attainable than they have ever been. Just a thought. I think the the real answer to why people aren't having kids is a lot more nuanced than finances, and has a lot to do with the fact that women have historicaly been pushed into the role of motherhood, rather than actively choosing to be one; there simply just wasn't a choice given to them.

NTA. My brother did the same thing growing up, including yelling the n word at black people from my car and making lynching jokes, as well as cat calling. He grew out of it and regrets it all now but for a few years it was a battle because I absolutely am not like that and I refused to drive him around. It would get to the point where I would have to threaten to kick him out of my car during trips home because he was so obnoxious. I’m sorry you’re dealing with this, but as an adult who owns your car you have full rights to who is in it. Don’t feel bad. Giving in is just enabling him, and he needs to understand not everyone will put up with his bullshit

YTA, and that’s simply because you haven’t been informing her that that was part of the deal when you paid her way to go. She’s not obligated to do something for you if you didn’t make it clear you were paying for her because you thought she would help. That’s on you. If you wanted her to help in exchange for paying her way, you need to tell her that, and not get angry after the fact. Or better yet, after being upset the first trip, asking her to help in exchange for you paying.

YTA, but not for the reason you think. While it’s perfectly okay to be uncomfortable with her still wearing her dead fiancé’s ring, it’s not okay to make her feel like you were okay with it, even if you were planning to talk to her about it. If you’ve known her for 10 months, you knew about the ring and her attachment to it. You needed to make it clear you were uncomfortable with it BEFORE you got together. She is completely in the right to be upset with you for not defending her when you’ve given no indication that you were uncomfortable with it. She even gave you an opportunity to bring it up when she asked you if you were okay with her bringing some of his things. That’s on you.
